official_measurement_examples.name: Listed-building point limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data's listed-building dataset states its point identifies a listed building but does not define the full area affected by the listing.

official_measurement_examples.name: Outline limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data's listed-building-outline dataset is incomplete and does not consistently show curtilage; it is explicitly an indicative guide requiring further checks before planning decisions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Curtilage legal test
official_measurement_examples.fact: Historic England Advice Note 10 explains that certain pre-July-1948 structures within a listed building's curtilage can be treated as part of the listed building, while the LPA or ultimately the court determines curtilage in disputed cases.

official_measurement_examples.name: Listed building consent separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Historic England states unauthorised works requiring listed building consent can be a criminal offence and that planning permission and listed building consent may both need separate consideration.

official_measurement_examples.name: Conservation-area data quality
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data states the conservation-area dataset is a work in progress, incomplete and contains duplicates while authoritative local-authority coverage is being expanded.

official_measurement_examples.name: Conservation-area controls
official_measurement_examples.fact: Historic England notes demolition or substantial demolition in a conservation area will usually require planning permission and tree works generally require six weeks' notice to the council.

official_measurement_examples.name: Local heritage distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Historic England's May 2026 Advice Note 7 describes local heritage lists as non-designated heritage assets; local listing must not be represented as national statutory listing.

official_measurement_examples.name: NPPF harm test
official_measurement_examples.fact: NPPF historic-environment policy distinguishes levels of significance and requires designated-heritage harm to be weighed under the applicable policy tests rather than treating designation as automatic development refusal.

core_rules: a listed-building point is not the legal extent of the listing
an indicative listed-building outline is not a definitive curtilage determination
listed building consent is distinct from planning permission
planning permission is not listed building consent
local listing is not national statutory designation
conservation-area membership is a planning consideration not automatic refusal
conservation-area dataset incompleteness must not be converted to absence
historic setting assessment must retain the affected asset and proposal context
curtilage depends on legal and factual assessment not proximity alone
unauthorised historic works must not be inferred lawful from age alone
heritage significance does not determine land ownership
heritage consent does not reserve development capacity
a building preservation notice is temporary protection not a completed listing decision
historic dataset geometry must retain source date and coverage limitations
no parcel heritage clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
